**My reasoning:**

My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. We have about 12 mu total, but I work 6 mu myself — my husband helps when he's not doing day labor in the city. The rest we rent out to a neighbor.

Around here, everyone grows wheat-corn. Winter wheat goes in around October, we harvest in June, then immediately plant summer corn on the same land. That's the rotation. I have done this every year since I was young. The soil here is flat loam — good for both crops. The county agricultural office pushed Jimai 22 wheat a few years ago and yields were decent, so I'll use that again. For corn, I buy Xianyu 335 seed from the town supply co-op — hybrid, everyone uses it.

Water is always a worry. We pump from the well for wheat — three times is what my neighbors do and what I do: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Corn gets rain mostly in summer but I'll pump once if July is dry like last year.

For fertilizer I apply compound fertilizer as base and top-dress with urea. I probably apply more than I should — my father always said more fertilizer means more grain — but I won't change that now.

Pesticides: wheat gets a herbicide spray in spring and one aphid/fungus spray before heading. Corn gets one herbicide pass right after emergence and one for stem borer if I see damage.

I use the rotary tiller before wheat planting. For corn I skip tillage — just direct sow into the wheat stubble after harvest to save time and fuel.
